locations.quote:
4.1 Generate Feedback Based on Guidelines

**Supervisors should be able to provide** their own scientific writing guidelines as well as conventions on the style of theses and proposals. Based on these guidelines, the LLM can provide formative feedback that is restricted to the aspects they cover.

4.2 Highlight Changes Across Iterations

**When the feedback tool has access** to previous iterations of the proposal or thesis, it can compare the latest submission with earlier ones, both at the level of the text itself and at the level of feedback items raised previously.

4.3 Compare Prompting Techniques and LLM Models

**Based on the writing guidelines**, the feedback tool needs to cover a range of aspects and topics across the thesis, from document structure and chapter organization to writing coherence, cohesion, and linguistic accuracy.

4.4 Integrate With Thesis Management

**Around 50 research groups** at TUM use Thesis Management to manage the thesis lifecycle. Within this portal, supervisors can record feedback that students can review and resolve in subsequent proposal iterations.

locations.quote: **Supervisors of theses spend considerable time on non-content-related feedback** such as document structure, coherence, and linguistic accuracy. Much of this feedback is repetitive across students and disciplines, draining supervisors and leaving less capacity for substantive research discussions.

**This thesis explores how large language models (LLMs) can generate formative feedback** on theses and proposals based on supervisor‑provided writing guidelines. Beyond a single draft, the tool also compares iterations to highlight improvements and surface persistent issues with more explanatory feedback.

**Bachelor’s and Master’s theses represent important final projects that students complete before graduating** [TP21]. Under the guidance of a supervisor, students conduct independent research and engage in depth with their chosen topic, applying the knowledge they have built throughout their studies to the academic world [AAM17].

**For students’ research proposals and theses, supervisors often provide feedback that is critical to their progress**. The supervisor takes the role of an experienced peer and coach in a mentoring environment, gradually increasing the student’s level of independence.

**Integrating large language models (LLMs) to assist supervisors with non‑content‑related feedback could improve the thesis writing process**. As Figure 1 illustrates, an LLM‑powered Reviewer works alongside the supervisor, evaluating the thesis against the research group’s writing guidelines and generating automatic formative feedback.
**This approach supports several modes of feedback generation**. In one mode, no LLM‑generated feedback is produced at all and all feedback comes from the supervisor.

locations.section: Transparency in the Use of AI Tools
locations.quote: In preparing this proposal, I made use of several AI-based tools across diferent stages of the writing process. For grammar and style correction, I used Grammarly to identify grammatical errors, improve sentence structure, and refne the overall writing style of my drafts. For translation and language enhancement, I used DeepL to translate passages between German and English and to improve the fuency of phrasings. For content generation and idea expansion, I used ChatGPT, OpenAI Codex, Claude, and Claude Code to reformulate sentences I had already drafted, expand on ideas I had outlined, and obtain suggestions for clearer phrasing. For coding assistance, I used GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT, OpenAI Codex, Claude, and Claude Code to support Typst formatting, generate snippets for fgures and macros, and resolve template-related issues. For citation assistance, I used Zotero to manage my references and to ensure proper citation formatting throughout the proposal. I have carefully checked all texts created with these tools to ensure that they are correct and make sense.
